import pytest
from rich.console import Console
from rich.panel import Panel
from rich.style import Style
import io

def test_panel_title_style_with_background_color():
    """
    Test that the title of a Panel respects the background color
    defined in the Panel's style, even when the title itself has
    inline styling.
    """
    console = Console(file=io.StringIO(), width=80, color_system="truecolor")
    panel_style = Style(color="white", bgcolor="blue")
    panel = Panel("Content", title='[bold white]Title[/bold white]', style=panel_style)

    # Render the panel to capture the output
    console.print(panel)
    output = console.file.getvalue()

    # The bug is that the background color from the panel_style is not applied
    # to the title area when the title has its own inline style.
    # We expect to see the blue background color applied to the title.
    # This is a simplified check, as parsing ANSI escape codes precisely
    # is complex. We'll look for the blue background color code (48;2;0;0;255m)
    # around the title text.
    # The exact sequence might vary slightly depending on how rich renders it,
    # but the blue background should be present.
    # A common sequence for blue background is \x1b[48;2;0;0;255m
    # and for bold white foreground is \x1b[1;38;2;255;255;255m
    # We expect the blue background to be applied to the title area.
    # The bug manifests as the blue background being absent from the title line.

    # Look for the blue background color code (48;2;0;0;255m)
    # and the bold white foreground color code (1;38;2;255;255;255m)
    # around the word "Title".
    # The exact position might vary, but the blue background should be active
    # when "Title" is printed.

    # This is a heuristic check. A more robust test would involve
    # parsing the ANSI codes, but for a regression test, checking for
    # the presence of the expected color sequence near the title is often sufficient.
    # The bug implies that the background color from the panel's style
    # is *not* applied to the title line. So, we assert that it *is* present.

    # Expected sequence for bold white text on blue background:
    # \x1b[48;2;0;0;255m\x1b[1;38;2;255;255;255mTitle\x1b[0m
    # Or, the background might be set first, then the foreground, then the text.
    # The key is that the blue background escape code should appear before "Title"
    # and be active for the title text.

    # A simpler check: the blue background color should be present in the output
    # on the line containing "Title".
    title_line_found = False
    blue_bg_found_on_title_line = False
    for line in output.splitlines():
        if "Title" in line:
            title_line_found = True
            # Check for the blue background color escape code
            # \x1b[48;2;0;0;255m is the truecolor blue background
            if "\x1b[48;2;0;0;255m" in line:
                blue_bg_found_on_title_line = True
            break

    assert title_line_found, "Title 'Title' not found in output."
    assert blue_bg_found_on_title_line, (
        "Expected blue background color (48;2;0;0;255m) not found "
        "on the line containing the Panel title. "
        "This indicates the panel's background style is not applied to the title."
    )
